out_items.name: Proper cooling time and temperature

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours. Chicken vegetable noodle soup=53F, 49F at the walk-in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. Put smaller amounts of soups or sauces in shallower pans, you may use ice paddles, place the food in a freezer for rapid cooling, place the food on ice bath and stir periodically, and other approved cooling methods. Both containers of soups were discarded during the inspection.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Cooling in Equipment
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: Large amounts of soups were placed in larger deep containers and the containers were filled close to the rims.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. Food discarded during the inspection.

out_items.name: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use

violations.title: Eating, Drinking, or Using Tobacco
violations.observation: Open drinking containers used or stored in a manner that may contaminate food, food contact surfaces or utensils.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees may have beverages in the kitchen areas as long as they are covered and consumed through a straw and stored in a manner that will prevent contamination to food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items. CORRECTED DURING THE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Working containers of poisonous and toxic materials are not properly labeled with a common name. Unmarked spray bottles containing cleaning chemical solutions were not labeled.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. CORRECTED DURING THE INSPECTION. This is a repeat violation, correct it permanently. Train employees to always label unmarked bottles and containers that are holding toxic chemical solution, to prevent unintentional use.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor in the walk-in freezer and walk-in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage.

out_items.name: Warewashing facilities installed, maintained and used; test strips

violations.title: Warewashing Equipment Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: The exterior surfaces of the mechanical warewashing machine are soiled with (limescale) that may decrease the effectiveness of the unit.
violations.corrective_action: A warewashing machine, the compartments of sinks, basins, or other receptacles used for washing and rinsing equipment, utensils, or raw foods, or laundering wiping cloths and drainboards or other equipment used to substitute for drainboards shall be cleaned before use, throughout the day at a frequency necessary to prevent recontamination of equipment and utensils and to ensure that the equipment performs its intended function and if used at least every 24 hours.

violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Clean these equipmernt frequently. Sunrise of Fairfax (Inspection Date: 05/27/2026) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Pasteurized foods used; prohibited foods not offered

violations.title: When to Use Pasteurized Eggs/Eggs Products in HSP
violations.observation: Raw shell eggs are used in the preparation of the following ready-to-eat foods without subsequent cooking in the facility that serves a highly susceptible population: poached eggs and other undercooked egg recipes.
violations.corrective_action: In a food service establishment that serves a highly susceptible population, pasteurized eggs or egg products shall be substituted for raw eggs in the preparation of foods such as Caesar salad, hollandaise, or Bearnaise sauce, mayonnaise, meringue, eggnog, ice cream, and egg fortified beverages and recipes in which more than one egg is broken and the eggs are combined.

out_items.name: Pasteurized eggs used where required

violations.title: Pasteurized eggs substituted for raw eggs in uncooked, egg-based recipes
violations.observation: Raw shell eggs are used in the preparation of the following ready-to-eat foods without subsequent full cooking: Poached eggs, and other undercooked egg recipes.
violations.corrective_action: Pasteurized eggs or egg products shall be substituted for raw eggs in the preparation of foods such as Caesar salad, hollandaise, or Bearnaise sauce, mayonnaise, meringue, eggnog, ice cream, and egg fortified beverages and recipes that where egg ingredient is not fully cooked and when the consumer is not informed by a disclosure and reminder statement.

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: Some of the unmarked squeeze bottles containing sauces and dressings were not labeled to identify contents.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc.

violations.title: Jewelry
violations.observation: Employees observed wearing jewelry such as watches on their arms and hands while preparing food.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall limit their jewelry to a plain wedding ring while preparing food. Food employees may not wear bracelets, watches, etc. because they can inhibit proper hand washing. CORRECTED DURING THE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: Milk crate(s) found used for the following purpose(s): Milk Crates are being used as shelves to store supplies above the floor, in dry storage areas and inside the walk-in refrigerator and walk-in freezer
violations.corrective_action: Milk crates, soda crates, and/or bread racks are not designed to store or elevate food, equipment, utensils, clean linens, and single-service items. Provide only ANSI-certified (such as NSF-listed) shelving units, storage units, or dunnage racks. Milk crates are not approved for such use.
